title: Amaranth vs. Quinoa: Nutrition Compared

seo.title: Amaranth vs. Quinoa: Nutrition Compared
seo.meta_description: Cooked quinoa and amaranth have similar protein; quinoa usually has a little more fiber, while amaranth stands out for calcium and a creamier texture.
seo.search_intent: Compare amaranth and quinoa for protein, fiber, minerals, calories, and cooking.

excerpt: Per 100 g cooked, quinoa is around 120 calories and 4.4 g protein; amaranth about 102 calories and 3.8 g. Quinoa usually has slightly more fiber, while amaranth contributes notable calcium and iron and cooks to a much creamier texture.
content_html:
Both are pseudocereals with good-quality plant protein, but they do not behave the same nutritionally or in the pot.

Protein and calories

Cooked quinoa is roughly 120 calories and 4.4 g protein per 100 g. Cooked amaranth is about 102 calories and 3.8 g protein. The protein difference is modest.

Fiber

Quinoa is commonly around 2.8 g fiber per 100 g cooked; amaranth is closer to 2 g.

Minerals

Amaranth is notable for calcium and iron, while quinoa contributes magnesium, phosphorus, and manganese.

Texture may be the deciding factor

Quinoa separates into distinct seeds. Amaranth releases more starch and becomes creamy, making it better for porridge-like dishes or compact fillings.

Quinoa for a fluffy grain texture; amaranth for a creamier result and a different mineral profile.

faq.question: Which has more protein?
faq.answer: Quinoa has a small cooked-weight edge, about 4.4 g/100 g versus roughly 3.8 g/100 g for amaranth.

faq.question: Which has more fiber?
faq.answer: Quinoa usually provides slightly more, around 2.8 g/100 g cooked.
